what_this_is: The layers that are not a stream. Each is a release of an external dataset, so the question is never how old it is - it is whether it is still there, still the file we accepted, still carrying the attribution and licence under which we may show it, and whether anybody has looked lately for a newer release. A layer with no expiry must not be reported as fresh either: silence about it is indistinguishable from neglect, which is what this register exists to end.

layers.what: the ground the maps are drawn on: river banks, municipality outlines, the city's frame
layers.why_no_expiry: the Sava and the Danube do not move, and a municipality outline changes by law rather than by the hour. An age limit here would report a fault every day and mean nothing on the day something actually changed.

provenance_as_the_file_carries_it.attribution: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com (public domain).

provenance_as_the_file_carries_it.name: basemap-belgrade

layers.what: how many people live near a station, as H3 hexagons - a modelled context layer, never a measurement, and labelled as one everywhere it appears
layers.why_no_expiry: it is a dated RELEASE of an external dataset. It becomes out of date when its publisher issues a new release, which is a thing to check for on a calendar, not a thing to infer from a file's modification time.
